A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Word4Per and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables. All pages were inspected, including v2's Appendices A-C; much of that appendix content is incorporated into v3's main text.

before.justification: V2 reports original ITCPR retrieval experiments, qualitative results and ablations, including Table 1 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V3 retains original retrieval experiments and reports additional template results, attention visualizations and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: V2's fine-tuning objective is L_irr + L_cmpm + L_id; v3's Equation (4) and Figure 2 specify L_sdm + L_id, removing implicit relation reasoning supervision. This is a limited revision to the reported first-stage objective. The renamed matching loss has equivalent mathematics, while TINet training and the two-stage retrieval framework remain.

E1.justification: Both versions use ITCPR, CUHK-PEDES, ICFG-PEDES, RSTPReid and the same combined IPR image pool. ITCPR retains 2,202 queries and 20,510 gallery images. Added annotation statistics, visualizations and timing procedures do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1/Table I retains the same main comparators, including Pic2Word, SEARLE-XL and Simple-CCReID-based Text+Model C. However, v2 Table B's ITC-loss comparison disappears. V3 Table IV also adds image-only and text-only comparators to the runtime/fusion comparison previously presented in Table D.

E3.justification: V3 Section V-E introduces timing measurements for 1,000 queries against 20,000 images and separately measures retrieval with pre-extracted gallery features. Table V adds two prompt configurations. Existing benchmark sizes, backbones, preprocessing, training budgets and stated evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the objective revision is identified under M1.

E4.justification: V3 adds attention-map analysis in Figure 9, fusion results for the existing qualitative cases in Figure 8, two template variants and a runtime breakdown. V2 Appendix C.2's ITC-versus-CMPM ablation is removed. Architecture, data-volume, fusion and real-word replacement analyses are otherwise largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. V3 retains point-estimate performance reporting; its additional measurements and descriptive dataset statistics do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Most retrieval values remain unchanged. ViT-B/16 L_Text Rank-10 changes from 68.574 to 68.584 in corresponding main, data-volume and fusion tables. V3 adds template results, including Rank-1 values 39.373 and 39.146, runtime measurements, caption statistics and attention/fusion findings. ITC results and some unique Rank-10 entries are omitted. These changes do not establish a same-setting performance gain under the revised objective.

T1.justification: V2 Equation (1), defining the masked-token implicit relation reasoning loss, is removed, and the total objective changes from v2 Equation (5) to v3 Equation (4). The remaining matching and TINet equations are mathematically equivalent after renaming. No new assumptions, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: introducing ZS-CPR, training Word4Per without CPR triplets, constructing ITCPR and outperforming comparison methods by over 10%. Additional supporting analyses do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 connects feature caching and model size to practical retrieval efficiency and describes fusion as providing the most stable qualitative results. It removes v2's specific limitation concerning the lack of explicit facial/body consistency preservation, and the appendix interpretation favoring identity-level grouping over treating individual image-text pairs as separate categories.

D1.justification: V3 specifies the runtime CPU, reports 15% additional training time per extra simultaneously trained TINet, and explains that token-length variations change TINet output dimensions. V2 Appendix B.3's detailed dataset and split counts are omitted. Existing optimizer settings, GPU information and promised code/data access remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds several references, including Vo et al.'s composed retrieval work and newer person-retrieval studies, while removing Chen et al.'s visiolinguistic-attention citation. Section II-B adds explicit positioning against Pic2Word's image-only training and SEARLE's LLM-assisted pipeline, emphasizing Word4Per's fine-tuning, semantic supervision and efficiency.

P1.justification: V3 substantially reorganizes the document, integrating most appendix methods, dataset descriptions and analyses into Sections III-V. Method and dataset passages are rewritten and subdivided, and an application section is added. The revision also introduces inconsistencies: the overview still says three losses, and the selected template's row reference conflicts with the inference description.

P2.justification: The document undergoes an ACM-to-IEEE layout redesign with widespread figure/table relocation and caption changes. New Figures 4 and 9 illustrate annotation and attention; Figure 8 adds fusion rows. V2 Table B disappears, Table IV gains comparator rows, and Tables II, V and VI omit Rank-10 columns.

improvement.justification: V3 integrates useful appendix material and adds informative template, attention and runtime analyses. However, it removes loss-comparison evidence and a concrete limitation, while revising the fine-tuning objective without reconciling the three-loss overview or explaining the almost entirely retained results. The PDFs do not resolve which objective produced those results, leaving the scientific benefit of the revision and its net quality direction uncertain.
